title: ownerOrNotGriefed check is vacuously satisfied when rewardRate is zero, allowing window manipulation against a stranded-dust budget
description:
The modifier's post-condition is `rewardRate >= rPre || endPre <= block.timestamp`. When `rPre == 0` (e.g., the most recent rate reset produced a floor-divided zero because `rewardBudget < windowDuration` — see CS-02 of the prior audit for the dust-stranding scenario), the `rewardRate >= 0` clause is vacuously true regardless of what the caller does. Any non-owner caller can invoke `topUp` / `pullAndRefresh` to reset `windowEnd` without any rate-floor protection.

Combined with the pre-existing floor-division issue, a griefer can deliberately trigger `_syncBudget` when only sub-windowDuration wei of phUSD is available, driving `rewardRate` to 0 as side effect, and then indefinitely extend `windowEnd` on every subsequent call without ever tripping the modifier. Once `rewardRate == 0`, the modifier is permanently disabled for that caller path until an owner-initiated intervention raises the rate back.
impact: Dust-stranding (prior CS-02 behavior) combined with a useless guard: when the stored rate is zero, the modifier does not protect against further window-extension griefing. The grief itself is low-impact because no rewards are accruing (rate is zero), but it prevents the schedule from ever self-correcting — each dust-top-up by owner can be immediately followed by a non-owner call that resets windowEnd to `now + windowDuration`, keeping emissions effectively stalled.
proof:
1. Assume `rewardBudget = 1 wei`, `windowDuration = 540 days = 46,656,000 sec`. `rewardRate = 1/46,656,000 = 0`. (This can arise naturally from CS-02 dust stranding or deliberately via an attacker-sized pull/top-up.)
2. Attacker calls `pullAndRefresh()`. rPre = 0. endPre = some past/future time.
3. `_syncBudget` runs, pulls dust from dispatcher. New rewardRate = still 0 (floor division). windowEnd = now + 540 days.
4. Post-check: `rewardRate (0) >= rPre (0)` is TRUE. Modifier passes.
5. Attacker can repeat indefinitely, keeping windowEnd perpetually at now + 540 days. No rewards are emitted.
suggested-fix: Tighten the modifier: require that if `rPre == 0` AND `rewardBudget > 0` going into the post-check, the caller must be owner OR the new rate must be non-zero. Alternatively fix the root-cause CS-02 floor-division issue — if the dust-stranding case is eliminated, this vacuous-guard case disappears. Simplest hardening: `require(msg.sender == owner() || (rewardRate > rPre) || (rewardRate == rPre && rewardRate > 0) || endPre <= block.timestamp, '...')` — i.e. zero-rate-to-zero-rate transitions must be owner-only even if 'rate didn't decrease' holds vacuously.
